rows: Budget balance and computational tractability may fail
Reserve prices sacrifice some efficient trades for seller revenue
Truthful and efficient, but not generally revenue-optimal
Winner determination is NP-hard; exact VCG is often impractical
Proposing side is favored; only that side gets strategy-proofness
Must restrict domain, randomize, add transfers, or accept dictatorship
IC + IR + efficiency + budget balance cannot all hold
Payment rule must make truthful probabilities optimal in expectation

Type safety / compiler enforcement: IC is a constraint that makes truth-telling a dominant strategy — the mechanism statically rules out profitable lying, analogous to a type system ruling out invalid operations

Abstraction layer: any indirect mechanism (sealed-bid auction, ascending auction, negotiation protocol) can be compiled down to an equivalent direct mechanism (ask types, run algorithm) — you don't lose generality by working at the direct level
Externality internalization: each agent pays the negative externality they impose on others — aligns private incentives with social welfare; exact analogue of Pigouvian taxation in public economics

No protocol satisfies all three "obvious" desiderata simultaneously (Pareto + IIA + non-dictatorship); in distributed systems: CAP theorem has the same flavor — no system satisfies all three of Consistency, Availability, Partition tolerance

Revenue-maximizing mechanism design = constrained optimization over allocation/payment rules subject to IC + IR; Myerson's ironing is a convexification step analogous to LP relaxation in integer programs
Impossibility result: efficiency + budget balance + individual rationality are jointly infeasible for bilateral trade — no market mechanism satisfies all three; trade-off must be made

Stable matchings as a fixed point of a deferred acceptance algorithm; runs in O(n²) and is used in NRMP (medical residency), FCC spectrum auctions, school assignment — a polynomial-time algorithm for a problem with no NE computation difficulty
Winner determination is NP-hard — the computational complexity of mechanism design for package bidding; practical systems use MIP solvers or approximation algorithms with bounded PoA

Proper scoring rules (Brier, log loss) are incentive-compatible mechanisms for eliciting probabilistic forecasts — paying log(p(true outcome)) makes truth-telling dominant; bridges to information-theory/ (log loss = cross-entropy)
